title: review: B4b v6 fix round 1: answer security review T-1562 (None-outcome control flow; JSON failures keep resume_hint)
spec:
Goal T-1403, wave 2, plan label B4b-v6-fix1. Fix round of T-1556 (constraints.fix_round_for = T-1556): T-1556 passed the gate on branch task/T-1556 (commit 7c76682); security review T-1562 returned request_changes with two in-scope comments on orchestrator/spawn.py. Work on the task branch cut from task/T-1556 (spawn.base_for cuts fix rounds from the fix_round_for branch). Change only what the two comments require. Locate every insertion point by symbol, never by line number.

Review comment 1 (med), spawn.py post_result, inside the `if triggered:` derivation block: when execute_outcome returns None the code posts the guarded failed write through worker_control.post_if_current and sets derived = True, but the next check `if outcome["ahead"] == 0:` is a plain `if`, so it subscripts None, raises TypeError, the generic except sends a spurious '<id>: derivation failed: ...' notify and suffixes the reason with ' (derivation failed: TypeError)' after the failed write already happened. Fix: the None case must end the derivation chain: make the ahead == 0 check an `elif` (the later branches already test `outcome is not None`), or move the None handling so no outcome subscript runs. Result for a None outcome: exactly one post_if_current('failed', {'reason': reason}) call, no notify, reason unchanged, run_worker returns status 'failed' (or 'superseded' when post_if_current returned False), exactly as the T-1556 spec item 9 states.

Review comment 2 (low), spawn.py post_result, the branch `elif derive and role == "execute" and resume_task is None and r.get("status") == "failed":` that follows the `if triggered:` block: with derive on, every failed execute run that is NOT a derivation candidate (budget cap, any JSON failure, pre_head None, cancel pending) now goes through post_if_current('failed', {'reason'}), which (a) drops resume_hint.partial_output that the legacy write keeps when r['output']['result'] is a string and (b) stamps registry status_reason 'non_json' on failures that were not non-JSON. The T-1556 spec asked for the guarded write only on the non-JSON fallback path. Fix: narrow that elif so only reasons starting with 'non-JSON output' take post_if_current; every other failed reason falls through to the legacy else branch (write_if_current with status, reason and resume_hint {'partial_output': result[:2000]} when output.result is a string), identical to derive off. worker_control.post_if_current itself is unchanged (its contract is pinned by tests/test_worker_control.py::test_post_if_current_single_lock_entry).

Tests (SPEC RULE): extend tests/test_spawn.py::test_derivation_falls_back_to_guarded_failed_write_or_superseded (it already exists on the branch) with two cases: (i) execute_outcome returning None: post_if_current is called exactly once with ('failed', {'reason': <the original reason>}), notify.notify is never called with a message containing 'derivation failed', the reason posted and returned has no '(derivation failed' suffix; (ii) derive True, role execute, fresh launch, run_claude returning {'status': 'failed', 'reason': 'budget cap', 'output': {'result': 'partial text'}}: post_if_current is not called, bus.update is called with status 'failed', reason 'budget cap' and resume_hint {'partial_output': 'partial text'}, and the registry entry's status_reason is not 'non_json'. Keep the four acceptance tests passing. Run tests/test_spawn.py and tests/test_worker_control.py in the foreground after committing; never background a command and never run the full gate; the daemon runs .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh.

Out of scope: worker_control.py behaviour, executor.py, daemon.py, any file not listed in scope. Rollback: git revert of the merge commit of this round.
acceptance: tests/test_spawn.py::test_execute_result_derived_from_git_state: passes exactly as specified for T-1556 (derived done with one bus.update, derived_done log_run once, execute_incomplete holds for no commits and for uncommitted changes through post_if_current with resume_hint dirty_in_scope/dirty_out_of_scope/head/partial_output, registry status_reason stamped, no second ensure_worktree call)

tests/test_spawn.py::test_derivation_falls_back_to_guarded_failed_write_or_superseded: passes: every T-1556 case still holds (derive False writes through write_if_current exactly as today with head_sha never called; reason not starting with 'non-JSON output', head_sha None, execute_outcome raising with reason suffixed ' (derivation failed: RuntimeError)', contracts.process raising, registry cancelling/cancelled/steering or a bumped steer_epoch returning 'superseded' with nothing written, a task already held 'cancelled' untouched, an earlier result with a commit still derived, resume_worker never calling head_sha, tool-escalation deriving from the final run_claude result with since equal to the head read before the first run, post_if_current returning False and nothing written when the worker already posted done/held/failed) AND the two new cases: execute_outcome returning None makes exactly one post_if_current('failed', {'reason': reason}) call with no 'derivation failed' notify and no reason suffix; a derive-on failed run whose reason does not start with 'non-JSON output' (for example 'budget cap') with a string output.result is written through write_if_current with resume_hint.partial_output equal to that string, post_if_current is not called and the registry status_reason is not 'non_json'

tests/test_worker_control.py::test_post_if_current_single_lock_entry: passes unchanged (post_if_current contract from T-1556: KeyError outside the lock for a held payload without hold_reason or resume_hint and for a failed payload without reason; exactly one outermost bus.locked entry; False and no write when not current or when the fresh status is done/held/failed or the registry is cancelling/cancelled/steering; an existing result commit does not block; exactly one bus.update otherwise; registry status_reason derived_done/execute_incomplete/non_json with registry status failed)

tests/test_worker_control.py::test_cancel_or_steer_pending_matrix: passes unchanged (True for registry cancelling/cancelled/steering, for a task held 'cancelled' and for a stale epoch; False for a running task with a current epoch; False without raising for a missing registry entry)

result.summary:
Both code fixes are correct and minimal. The test is thinner than the acceptance text implies.

Comment 1: `if outcome["ahead"] == 0` is now `elif`, so a None outcome ends the chain with one guarded failed write. There is no TypeError, no spurious notify, and the reason is unchanged.

Comment 2: the `elif` now requires a reason starting with 'non-JSON output', so other failures fall through to the legacy `write_if_current` branch. That branch keeps `resume_hint.partial_output`, as with derive off.

I reviewed the T-1556 branch diff against 7c76682. worker_control.py is unchanged.

comments.issue: The test now covers only two subcases (a None outcome on a non-JSON failure, and a budget cap). The old body only delegated to test_failed_without_reason_key_sets_default_and_resume_hint, and that call was dropped. The acceptance text lists many more T-1556 cases that nothing in this test exercises: derive False, head_sha None, execute_outcome raising with the ' (derivation failed: RuntimeError)' suffix, contracts.process raising, the cancel/steer superseded paths, resume_worker, and tool-escalation. Those paths are guarded only by the other test, test_execute_result_derived_from_git_state, if at all.

The assertion that the registry status_reason is not 'non_json' is vacuous. The fake run_claude upserts status_reason itself ('budget_cap'), and the test then reads back the value it wrote. It would pass even if post_if_current stamped 'non_json'. The `post.assert_not_called()` check does cover the behaviour, so the risk is low.
The later branches still carry a redundant `outcome is not None` guard, now dead after the `elif` fix. This is harmless. The guard on the final `elif outcome is not None` could be an `else`.
